diagnostic_evidence.quote: invertibility of $F$ requires that $f_V(p)$ is invertible

issues.failure_explanation: Every map f splits as f_V + f_{V^perp} for any subspace V, so the stated class is all manifolds. A linear encoder is injective on M only if f_V is injective (the preceding proposition says exactly this), and the encoder must also annihilate V^perp. The result is false without this hypothesis. For the circle f(theta)=(cos theta, sin theta), V=span(e_1) gives f_V=cos(theta), which is not injective, so the linear encoder cannot be injective on M.

failure_location.quote: (A linear--non-linear autoencoder can reproduce with $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ manifolds described by $f = f_V + f_{V^\perp}$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that f_V is injective (coordinates on V parametrize M) and that the encoder vanishes on V^perp; restate the class accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that a linear encoder suffices (summarized in the main-results list as justifying a linear encoder) is stated for a class that is not the right one.
issues.title: Linear–nonlinear autoencoder claim omits injectivity of f_V
issues.why_classification: A short standard hypothesis already identified in the supporting proposition repairs it; the examples (graphs, coil) satisfy it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$

issues.failure_explanation: Width n_l >= n_{l-1} is only necessary for an injective layer; sufficiency also needs full-column-rank W and an injective activation. The result is stated for ReLU-type universal approximation (Hanin–Sellke), and ReLU is not injective. Uniform approximation of an injective map does not give an injective approximant: for n=m=1, x+eps*sin(x/eps^2) is uniformly close to x but not injective. So the cited theorem cannot yield Epsilon_1=0. The statement's width n_in also contradicts the proof's n_in+n_out and the cited lower bound n_in+1.

failure_location.quote: each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the result with explicit conditions (injective activations, full-rank weights, and n >= 2m+1 or another embedding-type argument) and prove that an injective network approximating the embedding exists, or weaken to a conditional statement.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that a given architecture achieves null representation error (a central claim in the abstract and conclusions) is unsupported; Proposition prop:added-2 (generic manifolds) has the same gap.
issues.title: Width condition does not imply an injective encoder; proof of Theorem th:reduction invalid
issues.why_classification: A contained new argument or weakened hypothesis recovers a comparable result, but the stated sufficient condition and its proof must be replaced.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We conclude that $U$ is locally Euclidean
Global injectivity can be obtained by augmenting the solution set with parameters and time

issues.failure_explanation: The image U of a small ball is homeomorphic to the ball, but U need not be a neighbourhood of its point in the set M. Where different (t,mu) give the same state, other sheets of M pass through and M is not locally Euclidean there (e.g. a figure-eight curve, which is locally injective). Trajectories for different mu or time shifts can cross, so local injectivity does not exclude this. The proof also ignores boundary points of [0,T] x P (a manifold with boundary at best) and invokes compactness of P where only compactness of the ball is relevant.

failure_location.quote: the map $B_r((t^*,\mu^*)) \ni (t, \mu) \to u_N$ is injective $\forall (t^*, \mu^*) \in [0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$, with $r$ small enough

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume global injectivity of (t,mu) -> u_N (or work on the augmented set), and state the conclusion as a manifold with boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The a-manifold conclusion and the Menger–Nöbeling latent-dimension bound are unsupported under the stated hypotheses, which the paper itself concedes in the Observation and Conclusions.
issues.title: Local injectivity does not make the solution set a manifold
issues.why_classification: Theorem and proof go through under a stronger hypothesis, but the advertised scope (local injectivity only) is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, we can achieve the lowest latent size $n = a$.

issues.failure_explanation: The augmented set is the image of the compact set [0,T] x P, so it is homeomorphic to [0,T] x P, not to R^a. The n=a coordinates are (t,mu), which an encoder of u_N alone does not have. The augmented points live in R^{N+a} and the encoder would need (t,mu) as inputs, so the claim that M in R^N admits a latent size n=a does not follow. For non-injective (t,mu) -> u_N it is false in general (a figure-eight cannot be embedded in R^1).

failure_location.quote: follows that there exist a global homeomorphism to $\mathbb{R}^a$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the augmented-set homeomorphism correctly, and either require t and mu as encoder inputs or fall back to the 2a+1 bound for the unaugmented set.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed minimal latent dimension n=a, and the recovery from non-injectivity by augmentation, are unsupported for the actual autoencoder acting on u_N.
issues.title: Augmentation observation: false homeomorphism to R^a and unsupported latent size n=a
issues.why_classification: A corrected statement (augmented input or the 2a+1 bound) is available, but the n=a minimality claim is lost for the stated setting.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the assumption of \Cref{th:L_{F_n}}, the reduced problem

issues.failure_explanation: The bound is applied at Psi(u_n) for arbitrary u_n in R^n, and perturbed or network solutions leave Psi'(M). The suprema M_J and M_F are taken only over M, and L_{F_N} is used without being assumed or defined (only boundedness of F_N is assumed). Hence the global Lipschitz constant, and the well-posedness and Lyapunov bounds built on it, are not justified as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume F_N is Lipschitz and take the suprema over the set swept by Psi (a compact set containing the perturbed trajectories), or assume the bounds on R^N.
issues.overall_effect: Global Lipschitz continuity of F_n, and hence well-posedness and the Gronwall-based stability bounds, are not established under the stated assumptions.
issues.title: Lipschitz bound for F_n: hypotheses do not cover the points where it is applied
issues.why_classification: Adding local hypotheses and changing the domain of the suprema repairs it with no change to the method or conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$, so the bound on the timestep of the \node\ is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.failure_explanation: The nonzero eigenvalues of P*Lambda (P an orthogonal projector) are not eigenvalues of Lambda in general. For Lambda=[[-2,1],[1,-2]] (eigenvalues -1,-3) and P=e1 e1^T, A=-2. Hence the FE timestep bound for the n-ODE need not be at most that of the N-ODE. Also J_Psi' is n x N, so J_Psi'^T J_Psi' is N x N of rank n and cannot be inverted. The proposed loss enforces only J_Psi' J_Psi = I (a right inverse), not orthogonality of the projection.

failure_location.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the pseudo-inverse J_Psi = J_Psi'^T (J_Psi' J_Psi'^T)^{-1}, enforce range(J_Psi) = row space of J_Psi', and for symmetric Lambda use Cauchy interlacing to bound the spectrum of A within that of Lambda; otherwise drop the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The stated preservation of the timestep restriction for linear autoencoders (A-stability after reduction) is unsupported, and the construction that is supposed to realise it is ill-defined.
issues.title: Claim that the orthogonal-projection decoder preserves the eigenvalues of Lambda is false; decoder formula ill-defined
issues.why_classification: An interlacing argument for symmetric Lambda gives a contained repair, but the general claim must be restricted.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the fully data-driven training, by \Cref{th:fully_works}, we have that $\eps_{F_n} \to 0$ as $|\myw| \to \infty$ and $\Delta t_{\text{train}} \to 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Setting the loss residual to zero and subtracting the truncation identity gives Delta t * sum beta_p (N_F - F_n) = Delta t * tau + sum alpha_p (Psi'(u+zeta) - Psi'(u) + kappa). Dividing by Delta t_train shows the error in N_F is of order kappa/Delta t_train and zeta/Delta t_train, not kappa and zeta. For a first-order data generator zeta/Delta t_train does not even vanish. For general multistep operators the zero-residual recurrence for N_F - F_n also needs a root condition on the beta polynomial. The 'necessary' conditions are then used as sufficient to conclude eps_{F_n} -> 0 under independent limits.

failure_location.quote: A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove a sufficient bound including kappa/Delta t_train, zeta/Delta t_train and a stability condition on the multistep operator, and require the network accuracy to improve faster than Delta t_train (a coupled limit).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence of the fully data-driven N_{F_n}, and the joint limit |w| -> infinity, Delta t_train -> 0 in the global convergence theorem, are not established.
issues.title: Fully data-driven training: error in N_{F_n} divided by Delta t_train is ignored; 'necessary' conditions used as sufficient
issues.why_classification: A contained re-derivation with a coupled-limit hypothesis yields a comparable but weaker convergence statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $C_{1,\mu} > 0$ generally depends of the specific r.h.s. at hand and time integration scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound uses Lipschitz constants L_Psi and L_{F_n}, but the hypotheses only assume continuity. The time-discretization constant C_1 for dot w = N_{F_n}(w) depends on higher derivatives of the network N_{F_n}, which are not controlled by the sup-norm accuracy eps_{F_n}. It may grow as |w| -> infinity, so the conclusion that the bound tends to zero as |w| -> infinity and Delta t -> 0 is not justified without uniform bounds. Pointwise accuracy of N_{F_n} off the training data manifold along w_n is also assumed rather than shown.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume Lipschitz continuity (uniformly in w) and uniform bounds on the needed derivatives of N_{F_n} along the trajectory, so that C_1 is independent of |w|; state the uniform approximation region explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted convergence of the full error to zero is not supported by the stated hypotheses and proof, independently of the training issue in ISSUE-007.
issues.title: Global convergence theorem: missing Lipschitz hypotheses and uncontrolled constant C_1
issues.why_classification: Adding uniform-regularity hypotheses and a short argument repairs the proof, but the unconditional-looking limit statement changes to a conditional one.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: a simple strategy is to modify the loss function by adding a contribution whose minimization enforces conservation

issues.failure_explanation: The term is a sum of squared componentwise reconstruction errors. It is just the ordinary MSE and says nothing about the sum of concentrations. A conservation penalty would act on the aggregate, e.g. (sum_k [N_Psi(u_n)]_k - sum_k [u_N0]_k)^2. As written, adding it only reweights the existing reconstruction loss, so the claim that it enforces conservation is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Place the summation inside the norm, comparing the sum of reconstructed components with the conserved total.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the Test 3 model is trained to preserve the conserved total concentration, and the interpretation of the reported conservation error, are not supported.
issues.title: Proposed conservation loss does not enforce conservation
issues.why_classification: A local change to one loss expression fixes it without altering the method or results.
